question_text:
Build an 8x8 integer matrix filled with a checkerboard pattern of 0s and 1s, where the top-left entry is 0, entries alternate between 0 and 1 along each row and column, and no two horizontally or vertically adjacent entries share the same value. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

Construct a 5x5 floating-point matrix Z whose entries strictly below the main diagonal are 1.0 and every other entry (the main diagonal itself and everything above it) is 0.0. The result is a 2D array of shape (5, 5) with ones forming a triangle that excludes the diagonal. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

Given a 3x4 integer matrix Z whose entries are 0 through 11 in row-major order, return a 1D array of length 12 that lists Z's entries in column-major order (reading down each column from top to bottom, columns ordered left to right). (★☆☆)
Print the result.

Given a 1D vector Z of length 10 with arbitrary real entries, return the position of the smallest entry in Z as a single integer index in the range 0 through 9. If the minimum value happens to appear at more than one position, return the index of its first occurrence. (★☆☆)

Given a 1D float array Z, return a new float array of the same shape where each entry has been replaced by the largest integer that is less than or equal to it (so positives lose their fractional part toward zero and negatives are pushed further negative). (★☆☆)
Print the result.

Given two length-3 vectors A (all ones) and B (all twos), compute the value of ((A + B) * (-A / 2)) and store the final result in A, performing each intermediate step so that no new arrays are allocated and only A and B hold the working values. The final A should be a length-3 vector. (★★☆)
Print the result.

Given Z, a 1D float vector of length 10 whose entries are all 0.0, mark Z so that any subsequent attempt to assign into it (for example writing Z[0] = 1) raises a ValueError reporting that the assignment destination is read-only. The shape and dtype of Z must stay unchanged. (★★☆)

Build an 8x8 integer matrix filled with a checkerboard pattern of 0s and 1s, where the top-left entry is 0, entries alternate between 0 and 1 along each row and column, and no two horizontally or vertically adjacent entries share the same value. (★★☆)
Print the result.

Given a 1D vector Z of length 10 with arbitrary real entries, return a new length-10 vector whose smallest entry is exactly 0.0, whose largest entry is exactly 1.0, and where every other entry is linearly placed between them according to its original value's position in Z's value range (min-max normalisation to the interval [0, 1]). (★★☆)

Given n = 10 and p = 3, build a 10x10 floating-point matrix that starts as all zeros and then has exactly p of its 100 entries set to 1, with the p positions chosen uniformly at random without repetition from the full grid. (★★☆)
Print the result.

Given a 1D vector Z of 10 real numbers and a scalar target z = 0.5, return the single entry of Z whose value is closest to z (the entry whose absolute difference from z is the smallest across the whole vector). (★★☆)
Print the result.

Given a 2D array X of shape (100, 3) representing 100 observations across 3 columns, return a 3x3 array whose rows give the 25th, 50th, and 75th percentile values for each of the 3 columns (row 0 = 25th percentiles per column, row 1 = medians per column, row 2 = 75th percentiles per column). (★★☆)
Print the result.

Given a 2D array X of shape (100, 4) representing 100 observations across 4 variables (one per column), return the 4x4 symmetric matrix whose entry [i, j] is the Pearson correlation coefficient between column i and column j of X, with 1.0 along the diagonal. (★★☆)
Print the result.

Given a 1D integer array Z of length 50 whose entries are all non-negative, return the single integer value that occurs most frequently in Z. If two or more values share the highest frequency, return the smallest such value.
Print the result.

Given a 1D integer array a, return a new 1D array obtained by collapsing every run of consecutive equal entries down to a single occurrence (keeping the first entry of each run), so that no two adjacent entries in the output are equal. (★★★)
Print the result.

Given a 1D array values and a 1D integer array counts of the same length, return a 1D array where each entry values[i] is reproduced counts[i] times in order, reconstructing the original run-length-encoded sequence. (★★★)
Print the result.

Given a 2D integer array Z of shape (8, 5), return the subarray containing exactly those rows whose 5 entries are strictly increasing from left to right (each entry strictly greater than the one before it). The result is 2D with shape (k, 5) where k is the number of qualifying rows. (★★★)
Print the result.

Given a 2D array pts of shape (5, 2) holding 5 points in the plane (each row is an (x, y) pair) and a 3x3 homogeneous transform matrix T, return a (5, 2) array of the transformed points, where each output row is the (x, y) image of the corresponding input point under T applied in homogeneous coordinates. (★★★)
Print the result.

Given a 2D integer array Z of shape (10, 3), return the subarray containing only those rows whose 3 entries are not all equal to each other (i.e., drop any row in which all three columns hold the same value). The result is 2D with shape (k, 3) where k is the number of surviving rows. (★★★)
Print the result.

Build a 1D float vector Z of length 10 whose entries are all 0.0 except the entry at index position 4 (the fifth entry, counting from position 0), which holds the value 1.0. The result is a length-10 vector that is zero everywhere except at that one position. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

Given a 3x3 integer matrix Z whose entries are the values 0 through 8 laid out in row-major order, return a 1D integer array of length 3 whose i-th entry is the total of the three values in the i-th column of Z (one column total per output position). (★☆☆)
Print the result.

Build a 1D integer vector Z whose entries are the consecutive integers starting at 10 and ending at 49 inclusive, listed in strictly increasing order. The result is a length-40 vector. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

Given a 1D integer vector Z of length 5, return a 1D vector of the same shape whose i-th entry is the running total of Z's entries from position 0 through position i inclusive (so the first output entry equals Z[0] and the last output entry equals the total of every entry in Z). (★☆☆)
Print the result.

Given a 1D float array Z of length 10 with both positive and negative entries, return a new length-10 float array where each entry has been replaced by the nearest integer that is at least as far from zero as the original (so positive entries move up to the next integer and negative entries move down to the next more-negative integer, preserving sign). (★☆☆)

Given a square 2D matrix A of shape (2, 2) with integer entries, return a single scalar equal to the sum of the entries lying on A's main diagonal (those positions where the row index equals the column index). The result is a scalar, not an array. (★☆☆)

Given a 4D array arr of shape (batch, height, width, channels) representing a batch of color images in channels-last format, return a 3D array of shape (batch, height, width) where each output pixel holds the maximum value taken across the channel axis at that batch index and spatial location (one grayscale-style image per batch element, formed by collapsing channels via the per-pixel maximum).

Given img, a 3D array of shape (height, width, channels) representing a single color image in channels-last layout, return a 3D array of shape (channels, height, width) holding the same pixel data in channels-first layout: the channel axis is moved from the trailing position to the leading position, while height and width keep their relative order and follow it.

Given a 3D image array of shape (channels, height, width) representing a single color image in channels-first layout, return a 3D array of shape (channels, width, height) that holds the same image with its two spatial axes exchanged, so the result looks like the original reflected across its main diagonal.

Given a 3D image array of shape (channels, height, width) representing a single color image in channels-first layout, return a 3D array of shape (channels, height * 2, width) in which each original row of pixels is duplicated into two consecutive identical rows, stretching the image vertically to twice its original height while leaving channels and width unchanged.

Given a 5D array x_3d of shape (batch, channels, X, Y, Z) where each of the three spatial dimensions X, Y, Z is even, return a 5D array of shape (batch, channels, X/2, Y/2, Z/2) where each output entry is the maximum over a non-overlapping 2x2x2 spatial block of the input at the corresponding batch and channel index (3D max pooling with window 2 and stride 2 along every spatial axis).

You are given x_heads, a 4D array of shape (batch, heads, tokens, embedding_dim) representing multi-head attention output. Concatenate the per-head embeddings into a single embedding per token, returning a 3D array of shape (batch, tokens, heads * embedding_dim) where the head dimension is folded into the trailing embedding axis.

Given a 4D array arr of shape (batch, channels, height, width) holding a batch of channels-first color images, return a 3D array of shape (channels, height, batch * width) that lays every image side by side into one long horizontal strip: image 0 occupies the leftmost width columns, image 1 the next width columns, and so on, with channels and height preserved.

Define a custom NumPy structured dtype named color that describes an RGBA pixel as four unsigned byte fields, in the order r, g, b, a (each one byte, range 0-255). The result should be a dtype object usable to construct or interpret structured arrays where every element holds the four named color channels. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

Starting from a 5x5 array Z filled with ones, surround the existing values with a one-cell-thick border of zeros so the result is a 7x7 array whose outermost row and column on every side contain zeros and whose interior 5x5 region preserves the original ones. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

Given a 3x3 integer matrix Z, swap the top row with the bottom row so the row that was on top now sits at the bottom and the row that was at the bottom now sits on top. The middle row stays in place and the contents of each swapped row are kept intact. (★☆☆)

Given a 1D integer sequence with a mix of zero and nonzero entries, return the positions (indices) of every entry that is not zero, in their natural left-to-right order. The result should follow NumPy's convention for reporting nonzero positions of an array. (★☆☆)

Given a 10x10 array Z of zeros (float64), report how much memory the array's data buffer occupies in bytes and print that count, formatted as the string "<n> bytes" where <n> is the byte count. Count only the element storage, not Python or array-object overhead. (★☆☆)

Build a 5x5 matrix Z (shape (rows, cols)) in which every row contains the integers 0 through cols-1 in ascending order, so each row is identical and the column index equals the value stored. The five rows are stacked vertically to form the final 5x5 matrix. (★★☆)
Print the result.

Given the 1D array Z = np.linspace(-3, 3, 7), apply a ReLU-style clip so every negative entry becomes 0 while non-negative entries are left unchanged. The output keeps the original shape (7,) and dtype. (★★☆)
Print the result.

Given the 1D array Z = np.arange(12) (values 0..11), overwrite every third element starting at index 0 with the value -1, leaving all other entries untouched. The result is still a length-12 1D array of integers where the overwritten positions hold -1 and the remaining positions keep their original arange values. (★★☆)
Print the result.

Given the 2D array Z of shape (rows, cols) = (3, 4) holding the values 0..11 in row-major order, produce R of the same shape whose entry R[i, j] equals the running total along that row from column 0 up to and including column j. Each row is summed independently. (★★☆)
Print the result.

Given the 2D array Z of shape (3, 3) containing random integers in [0, 10), reorder its rows so that the values in column index 1 are in ascending order from top to bottom. Rows move as whole units; values within a row stay together. (★★☆)
Print the result.

Given two 1D float arrays a and b of the same length, where b may contain zero entries, compute the elementwise quotient a / b, but wherever the corresponding entry of b is zero, set that output position to 0 instead of producing inf or nan. The result has the same shape and dtype as a. (★★☆)
Print the result.

Define a NumPy ndarray subclass called NamedArray that carries an extra name attribute. The constructor takes an input array and an optional name string (default "no name"); the resulting object should behave like a normal ndarray while preserving its name through views and slicing. Instantiate it with np.arange(10) and the name "range_10". (★★☆)

Given a length-10 float32 array Z whose values are uniform random numbers in [0, 100), convert it to an int32 array Y that occupies the same underlying memory buffer (no new allocation for the data) and holds the truncated integer value of each original float. Y has shape (10,) and dtype int32. 
Print the result.

Given the 2D array Z of shape (5, 4) holding the values 0..19 in row-major order, and a length-5 random permutation p of the row indices, reorder the rows of Z according to p, writing the result back into Z so that the array is modified in place. The shape stays (5, 4). (★★★)
Print the result.

Given two 1D arrays A and B of equal length n, produce a length-2n array C in which the entries of A and B alternate position by position, so C[2i] is A[i] and C[2i+1] is B[i] for every valid i. (★★★)
Print the result.

Given the 2D array Z of shape (6, 7) containing random integers in [0, 5), build the summed-area table (integral image) I of the same shape, where I[i, j] equals the sum of all entries Z[i', j'] with i' <= i and j' <= j (the total of the upper-left rectangle ending at row i and column j). (★★★)
Print the result.

Given a 1D integer vector c of length n=6, build the n-by-n symmetric Toeplitz matrix T whose entry T[i, j] equals c[|i - j|]. The main diagonal therefore holds c[0], the first off-diagonals hold c[1], and so on out to c[n-1] in the corners. (★★★)
Print the result.

Given the 2D array Z of shape (rows, cols) = (4, 6) containing random floats in [0, 1), produce an integer array of the same shape where each entry is replaced by its rank within its row, with 1 assigned to the smallest value in that row and cols (=6) to the largest. Each row is ranked independently. (★★★)
Print the result.

Given a 1D integer vector I of length n=9 whose entries fit in 8 unsigned bits, build the n-by-8 matrix B of 0s and 1s in which row i holds the 8-bit binary representation of I[i] with the most significant bit in column 0 and the least significant bit in column 7. (★★★)
Print the result.

Build a 1D array Z that starts at 0 and steps by 0.5 up to but not exceeding 10, so the values are 0.0, 0.5, 1.0, ..., 10.0. The endpoint 10.0 must be included. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

Convert a Python nested list of two inner lists, each holding two integers, into a 2D NumPy array Z of shape (2, 2) preserving row order, so each inner list becomes one row of Z in the order it appeared. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

Given the 1D integer array Z = np.arange(5), produce a new array with the same shape (5,) and the same numerical values along its single axis, but with element dtype float32 instead of integer (so the new dtype is a 32-bit floating-point type and the values themselves are preserved as floats). (★☆☆)
Print the result.

Given the 1D array Z of shape (10,) containing random floats in [0, 1), reorder its entries so they are in ascending order, modifying Z in place rather than producing a separate sorted copy. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

Given two 1D integer arrays Z1 and Z2 of length 10, each containing random values in [0, 10), produce the sorted 1D array of values that appear in both Z1 and Z2, with each common value listed only once. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

You are given arr, a 4D array of shape (batch, channels, height, width) = (12, 3, 150, 150) holding 12 channels-first digit images. Tile these 12 images into a single composite image laid out as a 4-row by 3-column grid (rows fill first), producing a 3D channels-first array of shape (channels, 4 * height, 3 * width) = (3, 600, 450).

You are given arr, a 4D array of shape (batch, channels, height, width) = (6, 3, 150, 150) holding 6 channels-first digit images. Tile these 6 images into a single composite image arranged as a 2-row by 3-column grid (rows fill first), producing a 3D channels-first array of shape (channels, 2 * height, 3 * width) = (3, 300, 450).

You are given arr, a 4D array of shape (batch, channels, height, width) = (6, 3, 150, 150) holding 6 channels-first digit images. First downsample each image by taking the maximum value over every non-overlapping 2x2 spatial block, halving both height and width. Then tile the 6 downsampled images into a 2-row by 3-column composite (rows fill first), producing a 3D channels-first array of shape (channels, 2 * 75, 3 * 75) = (3, 150, 225).

You are given arr, a 4D array of shape (batch, height, width, channels) = (6, 150, 150, 3) representing a batch of channels-last digit images. Reorder the axes so the channel axis comes immediately after the batch axis, producing a 4D channels-first array of shape (batch, channels, height, width) = (6, 3, 150, 150) with all pixel values preserved.

You are given arr, a 4D array of shape (batch, channels, height, width) = (6, 3, 150, 150) holding channels-first digit images, and you use only the first 2 images arr[0:2]. Stack these 2 images vertically into a single tall image, and at the same time duplicate the result horizontally so the right half is an exact copy of the left half, producing a 3D channels-first array of shape (channels, 2 * height, 2 * width) = (3, 300, 300).

You are given x, a 4D float32 array of shape (batch, channels, height, width) = (2, 12, 8, 8). Compute, for each channel, a single mean value taken over the batch and both spatial axes (so 12 scalar means in total), then subtract that per-channel mean from every entry of the corresponding channel. The result has the same shape (2, 12, 8, 8) as x.

You are given x, a 4D array of shape (batch, channels, height, width) = (2, 3, 150, 150) holding channels-first digit images, with hs = 2 and ws = 2. Split each image's height into 2 stripes and its width into 2 stripes (forming a 2x2 grid of half-size sub-images per input image), then promote those sub-grid indices to the leading batch axis, producing a 4D array of shape (hs * ws * batch, channels, height / hs, width / ws) = (8, 3, 75, 75).

You are given rng, a NumPy random Generator seeded with a fixed integer so its output stream is deterministic. Produce a 1D array of length 3 containing the next three uniform floats in [0, 1) drawn from this generator. Because the seed is fixed, running the code repeatedly must yield the exact same three numbers. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 1D float array of length 3 that originally held a mix of finite floats and at least one NaN, but with every NaN entry already replaced by 0.0. Return Z so it can be inspected; the result must be a NaN-free copy of the original with the same shape, dtype, and ordering of the non-NaN values. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 10x10 float array whose outer ring (first row, last row, first column, last column) holds 1.0 and whose interior 8x8 block holds 0.0. Return Z as a framed pattern: a solid border of ones surrounding a hollow rectangle of zeros, with the original (10, 10) shape preserved. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

You are given a, a 3D array of shape (2, 3, 4) with arbitrary (uninitialized) contents, and Z, a new array built to match a's shape and dtype but filled entirely with zeros. Return Z.shape so the student can confirm the new array carries the same (2, 3, 4) shape as the source array. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 1D boolean array of length 4 with a mix of True and False entries. Return the total number of True entries in Z as a single integer count. The answer must reflect how many positions hold True, ignoring False entries entirely. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 1D integer array of the values 0 through 99, a scalar v drawn uniformly from [0, 100), and index, the position in Z whose value is nearest to v in absolute distance. Return Z[index] so that the printed result is the single element of Z that minimizes |Z - v|. (★★☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 1D integer array, and is_mono, a boolean flag set to True when every consecutive pair in Z satisfies Z[i+1] >= Z[i] (non-decreasing) and False otherwise. Return is_mono as a single boolean value summarizing monotonicity of the whole sequence. (★★☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 2D array of shape (3, 3) containing the integers 0 through 8 in row-major order, and R, the same array rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise about its center. Return R, a (3, 3) array where the original top row becomes the new left column and the original left column becomes the new bottom row. (★★☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 2D integer array with 4 rows and 3 columns where some rows are entirely zero. Return a 2D array containing only the rows of Z that have at least one nonzero entry, preserving the original column count and the original ordering of the surviving rows. (★★☆)

You are given labels, a 1D integer array of length 4 with class IDs in the range 0..K-1, K, the number of distinct classes (here 3), and onehot, a 2D array of shape (4, K) where row i contains a 1.0 in column labels[i] and 0.0 elsewhere. Return onehot so each input label becomes its corresponding one-hot row vector. (★★☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 2D integer array of shape (10, 3), k=4, and idx, a 1D array of 4 distinct row indices chosen uniformly at random from 0..9 without replacement. Return Z[idx], a 2D array of shape (4, 3) consisting of the 4 selected rows of Z in the order given by idx. (★★☆)

You are given Z, a 2D float array of shape (3, 3) whose third column is entirely NaN while the other columns are finite. Return a 1D boolean array of length 3 where entry j is True if column j of Z is filled with NaN values from top to bottom and False otherwise. (★★☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 2D float array of shape (4, 5) of random values in [0, 1), idx, a 1D array of length 4 holding the column index of the largest value in each row of Z, and out, a 2D array of shape (4, 5) that is zero everywhere except for a single 1.0 in row i at column idx[i]. Return out. (★★☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 2D integer array of shape (10, 4) holding the values 0..39 in row-major order, m=3, and idx, a 1D array of 3 distinct row indices drawn uniformly without replacement from 0..9. Return Z[idx], a 2D array of shape (3, 4) containing the chosen rows in the order they appear in idx. (★★★)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 1D float array of 1000 samples drawn from a standard normal distribution, the scalars lo and hi equal to the 5th and 95th percentiles of Z respectively, and Z_wins, a 1D array of length 1000 obtained by replacing every entry of Z below lo with lo and every entry above hi with hi. Return the tuple (Z_wins.min(), Z_wins.max()). (★★★)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 2D string array of shape (2, 3) where each row holds a name, a numeric string, and an integer string, and R, a structured record array of length 2 with named fields col1 (8-byte string), col2 (float64), and col3 (int64) populated from the columns of Z. Return R so each row is accessible by field name. (★★★)
Print the result.

You are given n=6 (the number of nodes), edges, a 2D integer array of shape (4, 2) where each row [u, v] is one undirected edge, and A, a 2D integer array of shape (6, 6) initialized to zero and then updated so that A[u, v] and A[v, u] are both set to 1 for every edge. Return A. (★★★)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 2D float array of shape (5, 6) of random values in [0, 1), k=2, idx, a 2D integer array of shape (5, 2) holding the column indices of the two largest values in each row of Z, and mask, a 2D integer array of shape (5, 6) that is zero everywhere except for a 1 at each (row, idx[row]) position. Return mask. (★★★)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 2D integer array of shape (6, 3) of random 0/1 values where some rows may be duplicates of each other, and uZ, a 2D array containing only the distinct rows of Z with the original column count preserved. Return uZ so duplicate rows of Z appear exactly once in the output. (★★★)

You are given Z, a 1D array of length 10 holding the integers 0 through 9 stored with dtype int32 (32-bit signed integers). Return Z so the printed result shows the sequence [0, 1, ..., 9] with its 32-bit integer dtype intact. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 1D float array of length 10 in which every entry is 1.0. Return Z so the printed result is a length-10 vector consisting of ten 1.0 values with the default floating-point dtype, with no zeros and no other values present anywhere along its single axis. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 1D float array of length 10 that started as all zeros and then had its entries at indices 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 (the slice 3:8) overwritten with 5.0. Return Z, a length-10 vector that is 0.0 outside that index range and 5.0 inside it. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 2D float array of shape (3, 3) of random values in [0, 1). Return a 2D boolean array of the same (3, 3) shape where each entry is True if the corresponding entry of Z is strictly greater than 0.5 and False otherwise. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 1D float array of length 10 holding 10 evenly spaced values strictly between 0 and 1 (both endpoints excluded), so the spacing matches what you get from splitting [0, 1] into 11 equal sub-intervals and taking the 10 interior breakpoints. Return Z. (★★☆)
Print the result.

You are given arr, a 4D uint8 array of shape (6, 3, 150, 150) representing a batch of 6 RGB digit images stored in channels-first (batch, channels, height, width) layout. Return a 4D array of shape (6, 150, 150, 3) that holds the same images in channels-last (batch, height, width, channels) layout by moving the channel axis to the trailing position.

You are given arr, a 4D uint8 array of shape (6, 3, 150, 150) holding 6 RGB digit images in (batch, channels, height, width) layout. Arrange the 6 images into a 2-row by 3-column grid (rows fixed at 2, columns inferred as 3) so each cell is one full image, returning a 3D array of shape (3, 2*150, 3*150) in (channels, grid_rows*height, grid_cols*width) layout.

You are given weights, a 2D integer array of shape (2, 4) representing per-token scalar weights for a batch of 2 sequences of 4 tokens each, and d=3, the feature dimension. Return a 3D array of shape (2, 4, 3) in (batch, tokens, features) layout where each weight is broadcast across all 3 feature slots so that output[b, t, :] equals weights[b, t] for every feature index.

You are given hwcs, a 4D uint8 array of shape (2, 150, 150, 3) holding 2 RGB digit images in (batch, height, width, channels) layout. Concatenate the 2 images side by side along the width axis, returning a 3D array of shape (150, 2*150, 3) in (height, batch*width, channels) layout so the second image appears immediately to the right of the first.

You are given x, a 4D uint8 array of shape (2, 6, 150, 150) in (batch, channels, height, width) layout where the 6 channels are conceptually two stacked halves of 3 channels each. Split the channel axis into its first 3-channel half and its second 3-channel half, returning a 5D array of shape (2, 2, 3, 150, 150) in (split, batch, channels_per_half, height, width) layout whose two slices along the leading split axis are part1 and part2.

You are given img_a and img_b, two 3D uint8 arrays each of shape (150, 150, 3) in (height, width, channels) layout. Treat them as a batch of 2 images and concatenate them side by side along the width axis, returning a 3D array of shape (150, 2*150, 3) in (height, batch*width, channels) layout so img_b sits immediately to the right of img_a.

You are given arr, a 4D uint8 array of shape (6, 3, 150, 150) holding 6 RGB digit images in (batch, channels, height, width) layout. Stack the 6 images on top of each other along the height axis, returning a 3D array of shape (3, 6*150, 150) in (channels, batch*height, width) layout so all 6 images form a single tall column with image 0 on top and image 5 on the bottom.

You are given Z, a 2D array of shape (5, 5) filled with random values drawn from the uniform distribution on [0, 1). Rescale Z so that its overall mean becomes 0 and its overall standard deviation becomes 1, computing those statistics across all 25 entries (not per-row or per-column). The result should be a (5, 5) array of the same dtype. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 1D complex-valued array of shape (2,) whose two entries each carry a real part and an imaginary part. Produce two separate real-valued arrays of shape (2,): the first contains the real components of each entry, and the second contains the imaginary components. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 1D array of shape (30,) filled with random values drawn from the uniform distribution on [0, 1). Compute the arithmetic mean across all 30 entries and return the result as a single floating-point scalar (sum of the entries divided by 30). (★☆☆)

Build Z, a 3D array of shape (3, 3, 3) filled with random values drawn from the uniform distribution on [0, 1). The result is a single array of that shape and a floating-point dtype. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

Build Z, a 1D floating-point array of shape (5,) containing 5 evenly spaced values that start at 0 and end at 1 inclusive, with equal spacing between consecutive entries. The first entry must be exactly 0.0, the last entry must be exactly 1.0, and entries in between fill in at uniform steps. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 1D integer array of shape (10,) containing the values 0 through 9 in order. Produce a single scalar equal to the total of all entries of Z. The output is one integer value, not an array. (★★☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 2D array of shape (4, 3) containing the integers 0 through 11 in row-major order, along with perm, a 1D array of shape (4,) holding a random permutation of the row indices 0 through 3. Return a (4, 3) array whose rows are the rows of Z reordered according to perm, so each output row is one row of Z taken in the order specified by perm. (★★☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 2D square array of shape (5, 5) containing the integers 0 through 24 in row-major order. Return d, a 1D array of shape (4,) containing the entries that sit one position above the main diagonal of Z, that is the entries Z[i, i+1] for i in 0 through 3, in that order. (★★☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 2D integer array of shape (4, 5) that acts as a binary mask: most entries are 0 and a few are 1. Return coords, a 2D array of shape (k, 2) where k is the number of nonzero entries in Z; each row of coords gives the (row, column) index of one nonzero entry. (★★☆)

Build Z, a 1D structured array of length 10 whose dtype has two top-level fields: 'position', itself a nested structure with float fields 'x' and 'y'; and 'color', a nested structure with float fields 'r', 'g', and 'b'. All entries should be zero-initialized. (★★☆)
Print the result.

You are given z, a 1D floating-point array of shape (3,) holding three real-valued logits. Return softmax, a 1D array of the same shape whose entries are non-negative and sum to 1, where each output entry is proportional to the exponential of the corresponding input entry. (★★☆)
Print the result.

You are given x, a 1D integer array of shape (7,) containing the values 0 through 6 in order. Return W, a 2D array of shape (5, 3) where each row is a contiguous length-3 window of x starting at successive positions, so W[i] equals x[i:i+3]. (★★☆)
Print the result.

You are given s, a StringIO object holding CSV-formatted text with 3 rows and 5 comma-separated columns of integers, where some entries are blank (whitespace only). Parse it into Z, a 2D integer array of shape (3, 5), with every blank entry replaced by 0. (★★☆)

You are given A, a 2D array of shape (5, 5) containing the integers 1 through 25 in row-major order, and an integer k (here -2) which may be positive, zero, or negative. Return diag_k, a 1D array containing the entries A[i+|k|, i] when k is negative or A[i, i+k] when k is non-negative, taken along the k-th diagonal of A in order of increasing index. (★★★)

You are given a, a 1D integer array of shape (10,) containing the values 0 through 9 in order, and an integer k (here 3). Return d, a 1D array of length 10 - k whose entries are the result of repeatedly taking pairwise consecutive differences of a a total of k times. (★★★)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 2D integer array of shape (5, 8) whose entries are random integers from 0 to 5 inclusive. Return counts, a 1D array of shape (5,) where counts[i] is the number of distinct values that appear in row i of Z. (★★★)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 1D integer array of shape (20,) containing the values 0 through 19 in order, and a window size n (here 3). Return a 1D array of length 20 - n + 1 whose i-th entry is the arithmetic mean of the n consecutive entries of Z starting at index i. (★★★)

You are given Z, a 2D floating-point array of shape (10, 10) with entries drawn from the uniform distribution on [0, 1). Return rank, a single integer scalar giving the rank of Z as a matrix (the number of linearly independent rows or columns). (★★★)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 1D integer array of shape (10000,) containing a random permutation of the values 0 through 9999, and an integer n (here 5). Return a 1D array of length n containing the n largest values of Z. The output ordering need only contain those n values; their internal order is not constrained. (★★★)
Print the result.

Build Z, a 2D integer array of shape (8, 8) whose entries form a checkerboard: Z[i, j] is 0 when i + j is even and 1 when i + j is odd, with the top-left entry Z[0, 0] equal to 0. Adjacent cells (horizontally or vertically) must hold opposite values, producing the classic alternating 0/1 grid. (★☆☆)

Build Z, a 1D floating-point array of shape (10,) in which every entry is 0.0. The result is a single null vector of length 10 with a floating-point dtype, where each of the 10 positions holds the value zero. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 1D integer array of shape (30,) containing the values 0 through 29 in order. Return a 1D boolean array of the same shape whose i-th entry is True exactly when Z[i] is divisible by 3. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 2D floating-point array of shape (4, 4) with entries drawn from the uniform distribution on [0, 1). Return a single scalar equal to the sum of the four main-diagonal entries Z[i, i] for i in 0 through 3. (★☆☆)

You are given A, a 2D integer array of shape (2, 2) containing the values 1 through 4 in row-major order. Return a 2D array of shape (2, 2) in which the row and column axes have been swapped, so the output entry at position (j, i) equals A[i, j]. (★☆☆)

You are given x, a 4D array of shape (batch, channels, height, width) of channels-first images, plus integer subgrid factors hs and ws (here both 2) that evenly divide height and width. First produce a packed intermediate of shape (hs * ws * batch, channels, height / hs, width / ws) by splitting each image into an hs-by-ws spatial grid and folding both subgrid axes plus batch into the leading axis. Then invert that step to recover the original (batch, channels, height, width) array.

You are given list_of_tensors, a 4D array of shape (batch, channels, height, width) holding several channels-first images stacked along the leading axis. Return a 4D array of shape (batch, height, width, channels) in which the channels axis has been moved from position 1 to the trailing position, converting each image from channels-first to channels-last layout while keeping the batch ordering.

You are given x, a 4D floating-point array of shape (batch, channels, height, width). For each (batch, channels) pair, compute the mean over the spatial axes (height, width) and subtract that scalar mean from every spatial location of the corresponding (batch, channel) feature map. Return a 4D array of shape (batch, channels, height, width) in which each per-image, per-channel slice now has zero spatial mean.

You are given img, a 3D array of shape (channels, height, width) representing a single channels-first RGB image. Return a 2D array of shape (height, channels * width) in which the per-channel 2D slices have been laid out side-by-side along the width axis, so the three color planes appear as three grayscale panels stacked horizontally in channel order.

You are given x, a 4D array of shape (batch, channels, height, width) whose channels axis has an even length and is interpreted as interleaved pairs (channels = c_in * 2, with the two members of each pair sitting at consecutive channel positions). Return a 5D array of shape (2, batch, c_in, height, width) whose leading axis selects between the two interleaved sub-streams: index 0 collects every even-indexed channel and index 1 collects every odd-indexed channel.

You are given four channels-last images img_a, img_b, img_c, img_d, each a 3D array of shape (height, width, channels) with identical shape. Combine them into a single 3D array of shape (2 * height, 2 * width, channels) arranged as a 2-by-2 spatial grid: img_a and img_b occupy the top row (left and right), and img_c and img_d occupy the bottom row (left and right).

You are given img, a 3D array of shape (channels, height, width) representing a single channels-first image. First add a leading singleton batch axis to produce shape (1, channels, height, width). Next flatten the channel and spatial axes together to produce a 2D array of shape (1, channels * height * width) suitable for a fully-connected classifier. Finally drop the leading singleton axis to produce a 1D array of length channels * height * width.

Build a 4x4 2D array where every entry equals its own row index, so each row holds a single repeated integer value and that value equals the row's position from top to bottom. The result must have integer dtype and shape (4, 4). (★☆☆)

You are given Z, a 3x3 integer matrix containing the values 0 through 8 arranged row by row. For each row, compute the successive differences between adjacent column entries, producing a 2D array of shape (3, 2) where entry (i, j) equals Z[i, j+1] - Z[i, j]. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

Build a 5x5 floating-point matrix where every entry on or above the main diagonal equals 1.0 and every entry strictly below the main diagonal equals 0.0. The result is the upper-triangular indicator of a 5x5 matrix. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

Build a 2D integer matrix of shape (3, 3) whose entries, read row by row from top-left to bottom-right, are the consecutive integers 0 through 8 in row-major order, so the smallest value sits in the top-left cell and the largest value sits in the bottom-right cell. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

Draw a 1D vector of 10 random floats in [0, 1), then return the same values reordered from smallest to largest. The result has shape (10,) with entries in non-decreasing order. (★★☆)
Print the result.

You are given A and B, two 1D integer arrays of length 5 with entries in {0, 1}. Report two booleans: first, whether A and B agree elementwise within floating-point tolerance, and second, whether A and B have the same shape and exactly equal values. Print each boolean on its own line. (★★☆)
Print the result.

You are given labels, a 1D integer array of length 5 holding class indices in the range 0..K-1, and values, a 1D lookup table of length K indexed by class. Produce a 1D array of length 5 whose i-th entry is the lookup-table value at position labels[i]. (★★☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 2D integer array of shape (3, 3) whose first and second rows happen to be identical. Return a 2D array containing each unique row of Z exactly once, with rows ordered lexicographically and the original column count preserved. (★★☆)

You are given a and b, two 1D arrays of equal length 3. Return a single 1D array of length 6 whose entries alternate between a and b starting with a[0], so the result is [a[0], b[0], a[1], b[1], a[2], b[2]]. (★★☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 1D vector of 10 random floats in [0, 1). Rescale Z by a single positive constant so that the resulting vector has Euclidean length equal to 1, i.e. the square root of the sum of its squared entries equals 1. The result has shape (10,) and points in the same direction as Z. (★★☆)
Print the result.

For n = 5, build an n x n floating-point permutation matrix: each row and each column contains exactly one 1.0 and the remaining entries are 0.0, with the positions of the 1.0s determined by a uniformly random permutation of {0, 1, ..., n-1}. The result has shape (5, 5). (★★☆)
Print the result.

You are given X = [0, 1, 2, ..., 7] and Y = X + 0.5, two 1D arrays of length 8. Build the 8x8 Cauchy matrix C with C[i, j] = 1 / (X[i] - Y[j]), then return the determinant of C as a single scalar. (★★☆)
Print the result.

You are given X, a 2D array of shape (5, 4) whose 5 rows are treated as 4-dimensional vectors. Return the 5x5 cosine-similarity matrix S where S[i, j] equals the dot product of rows i and j of X divided by the product of their Euclidean lengths. The diagonal of S is 1 and S is symmetric. (★★☆)
Print the result.

You are given A and B, two 2D arrays of shape (5, 5) with random entries in [0, 1). Return a 1D array of length 5 whose i-th entry equals the i-th diagonal entry of the matrix product A @ B, i.e. the dot product of row i of A with column i of B. (★★★)

You are given y, a 1D integer label vector of length 5 whose values lie in {0, 1, ..., C-1} where C = y.max() + 1 = 3. Return a 2D integer array of shape (5, 3) whose i-th row is the C-dimensional one-hot indicator of y[i]: a 1 in column y[i] and 0s elsewhere. (★★★)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 2D array of shape (5, 3) with non-negative entries. Return a 2D array of the same shape (5, 3) where each row of Z is rescaled by a single positive constant so that its entries sum to 1; for any row whose sum is 0, leave that row as all zeros to avoid division by zero. (★★★)
Print the result.

You are given X, a 2D array of shape (6, 5) whose 6 rows are treated as 5-dimensional vectors. Return the 6x6 cosine-similarity matrix S where S[i, j] equals the dot product of rows i and j of X divided by the product of their Euclidean lengths. The diagonal of S is 1 and S is symmetric. (★★★)
Print the result.

You are given B, a 2D binary array of shape (6, 8) whose 6 rows are interpreted as subsets of an 8-element universe (a 1 at column k means element k is in the set). Return the 6x6 symmetric Jaccard-distance matrix J where J[i, j] = 1 - |row_i intersect row_j| / |row_i union row_j|; when the union of two rows is empty, substitute the denominator with 1 so the entry stays 1 instead of becoming NaN. (★★★)
Print the result.

Build a 2D array of shape (3, 3) with boolean dtype in which every one of the 9 entries holds the value True. The result must use the bool dtype (not integer or float) and contain no False entries anywhere in the matrix. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 1D vector of 10 random floats in [0, 1). Return the same vector but with the single entry that holds the largest value replaced by 0; all other entries keep their original values. The result has shape (10,). (★★☆)

Build a 2D floating-point identity matrix of shape (3, 3): the three entries on the main diagonal equal 1.0 and the six off-diagonal entries equal 0.0. The result is the 3x3 multiplicative identity for matrix multiplication. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

You are given Z, a 1D integer vector of length 50 containing the values 0, 1, 2, ..., 49 in order. Return a 1D vector of the same length whose entries appear in the reverse order, so the result starts at 49 and ends at 0. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

You are given a 2D array of shape (5, 3) filled with 1.0 and a 2D array of shape (3, 2) filled with 1.0. Return their matrix product as a 2D array of shape (5, 2), where each output entry is the sum of three 1*1 products. (★☆☆)
Print the result.

You are given A, a 2D array of shape (2, 2) with integer entries arranged row by row. Return a 1D array of length 2 whose j-th entry equals the sum of the j-th column of A, i.e. collapse the first axis by addition while keeping the second axis intact. (★☆☆)

You are given patches, a 4D array of shape (h*w, p1, p2, channels) = (225, 10, 10, 3) containing the 225 non-overlapping 10x10 RGB tiles of a 150x150 image, listed in row-major order with h = 15 tile-rows and w = 15 tile-columns. Reassemble the original image as a 3D array of shape (h*p1, w*p2, channels) = (150, 150, 3) by placing each tile back at its (row, column) position in the grid.

You are given a list [img, img] of two identical 3D images, each of shape (height, width, channels) = (150, 150, 3). Produce a single 3D array of shape (2*height, width, channels) = (300, 150, 3) by interleaving the two images row-by-row: row 0 of the output is row 0 of the first image, row 1 is row 0 of the second image, row 2 is row 1 of the first image, and so on.

You are given img, a 3D channels-first image of shape (channels, height, width) = (3, 150, 150) holding a single digit. Produce a 3D array of shape (channels, 2*height, width) = (3, 300, 150) whose top half along the height axis is a copy of img and whose bottom half is another copy of img, so the digit appears twice stacked vertically with channels and width preserved.

You are given x, a 4D array of shape (batch, channels, height, width) = (2, 12, 8, 8). Return a single scalar (a 0D array) equal to the sum of every entry of x across all four axes, suitable as a loss sanity-check.

You are given arr, a 4D channels-first batch of shape (batch, channels, height, width) = (6, 3, 150, 150) holding 6 digit images. Split the batch axis 6 into b1 = 2 rows and b2 = 3 columns of images, then tile them into a single 3D channels-first canvas of shape (channels, b1*height, b2*width) = (3, 300, 450), where the i-th batch image lands in row i // 3 and column i % 3 of the 2x3 grid.

You are given arr, a 4D channels-last batch of shape (batch, height, width, channels) = (6, 150, 150, 3) holding 6 digit images. Split the batch axis 6 into r = 3 rows and nc = 2 columns of images, then tile them into a single 3D channels-last canvas of shape (r*height, nc*width, channels) = (450, 300, 3), where the i-th batch image lands in row i // 2 and column i % 2 of the 3x2 grid.

You are given seq, a 3D array of shape (batch, tokens, heads*embedding_dim) = (2, 12, 8) representing a transformer sequence whose trailing axis is the concatenation of 8 attention heads. With heads = 8, split that trailing axis into a heads axis and a per-head embedding_dim axis (so embedding_dim = 1 here) and move the heads axis next to the batch, producing a 4D array of shape (batch, heads, tokens, embedding_dim) = (2, 8, 12, 1).

You are given x, a 4D array of shape (batch, channels, height, width) = (2, 3, 150, 150) holding two channels-first images. First apply a 2x2 maximum pooling on the spatial axes, taking the maximum value within each non-overlapping 2x2 window of height and width so each spatial axis is halved. Then flatten the channel axis together with the two pooled spatial axes into a single trailing feature axis, returning a 2D array of shape (batch, channels * (height/2) * (width/2)) = (2, 16875).

You are given img, a 3D array of shape (channels, height, width) = (6, 150, 150) in channels-first layout where channels is even. Treat the channels axis as consecutive pairs of length 2, split it into two halves such that within every pair the first member goes into the first half and the second member goes into the second half, and promote that within-pair index to a new leading axis. Return a 4D array of shape (2, channels/2, height, width) = (2, 3, 150, 150).

You are given arr, a 4D array of shape (batch, height, width, channels) = (2, 3, 8, 5) in BHWC layout. Reinterpret the width axis as a (remaining_width, factor) pair where factor = 4 (so remaining_width = 2), then merge that factor of 4 into the height axis as its outer index, producing a 4D array of shape (batch, factor * height, remaining_width, channels) = (2, 12, 2, 5).
